steps.context: 3 treated vs 3 control liver samples. At the low end of the replicate range the two count models are known to disagree on some genes, most often at low counts, so their overlap is the honest confidence statement the research question asks for. edgeR uses its own filterByExpr and TMM normalization — that is intentional, since the point is an independent pipeline rather than a re-skin of the DESeq2 one.

grounding.reason: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test is the permitted alternative (M-0003) under R-0001@9a17 and is run here as the second method for the robustness check; the overlap is reported per R-0042@54e1. Choice stated: DESeq2 remains the primary result, edgeR the robustness check.

steps.description: Assemble the final report. Order it so the confidence framing precedes the gene list: (1) the design and contrast as stated (condition, treated, control; 3 vs 3; single batch; no length offset applied to the Salmon gene-level counts, with the consequence that isoform-usage shifts can masquerade as differential expression); (2) the expected-power statement from T1S2 — the fold change detectable at 80% power with n=3 per group over the assumed BCV range, plus the plain statement that at three replicates a count model recovers only a minority of true effects and that absence from the list is not evidence of no change; (3) the fit diagnostics — MA plot on the shrunken LFC, dispersion plot, and the p-value histogram with its shape described; (4) the DESeq2 gene table ranked by shrunken log2 fold change, carrying unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE side by side, restricted to padj < 0.05; (5) the two-method overlap from T1S4, naming the intersection as the high-confidence set; (6) the reproducibility record — sessionInfo, all package versions, the design formula, the contrast, the thresholds, the number of genes tested and the number called per contrast, and any random seed used. The lost length offset is stated as a limitation with its concrete consequence
An empty or near-empty significant set is reported as such, with no threshold relaxation

plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control DE with power assessment
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000-gene x 6-sample gene-level count matrix (counts.csv) from Salmon plus a 6-row metadata table with a single condition column: 3 drug-treated vs 3 control human liver samples, unpaired, single batch. The research question is two-part — which genes differ, and how much confidence three replicates per group support — so the plan is a single track: sample-structure QC, then a DESeq2 negative-binomial Wald test with apeglm shrinkage and BH adjustment at alpha 0.05, then an independent edgeR quasi-likelihood re-analysis of the same counts and design as a robustness check, then a report that puts the power statement and the overlap of the two methods in front of the gene table.

Two facts of the profile drive method choices. First, the counts are 'gene-level counts from Salmon as delivered; the record does not say whether the length correction occurred', and no quant.sf files or average-transcript-length table are present in the inputs. tximport cannot be run on a gene-level table, and a length offset must not be invented — so the model is fit on the counts as delivered without a length offset, and the report states that the length offset is lost and that a shift in isoform usage can appear as differential expression. Second, n=3 per group is at the low end. That does not change the method (DESeq2/edgeR both control FDR at 2-11 replicates) and explicitly does not license loosening alpha; it changes what may be concluded. So the design step computes an expected-power curve from the closed-form relation between replicate count, depth, dispersion and fold change (RNASeqPower and PROPER are not installed, so the closed form is used), and the DE and report steps carry that caution: at three replicates a count model recovers only a minority of true effects, mostly those with |log2FC| above ~1, and absence from the significant list is not evidence of no change.

No enrichment step is planned — the question asks which genes differ and with what confidence, not which pathways; adding gene-set analysis would be unasked scope, and with the DE set likely small it would be unreliable anyway.

grounding.reason: Fixed-effects two-group design with 3 replicates per group: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage per R-0001@9a17 and R-0009@310d; BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering per R-0010@6072 and R-0166@bbcd; low-power caution per R-0017@8a47

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood robustness check
steps.question: Does an independent count model (edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test) on the same treated-vs-control counts call the same genes as DESeq2, and how large is the intersection?
steps.description: Re-analyse the same 12,000-gene count matrix and the same treated-vs-control design with edgeR as a second, independent method. Build a DGEList, apply filterByExpr with the condition group, compute TMM normalization factors, estimate dispersions, fit glmQLFit and run glmQLFTest for the treated-vs-control contrast, adjusting with BH at 0.05. Then compare against the DESeq2 result from T1S3: report the number of significant genes from each method, the size of the intersection, and the genes called by only one method labelled with that method. Produce the concordance of log2 fold changes between the two methods (scatter plus correlation over the commonly tested genes) and a rank-agreement summary. Treat the intersection as the high-confidence set and the single-method calls as a clearly labelled secondary set. Do not report the union as the result.
steps.context: 3 treated vs 3 control liver samples. At the low end of the replicate range the two count models are known to disagree on some genes, most often at low counts, so their overlap is the honest confidence statement the research question asks for. edgeR uses its own filterByExpr and TMM normalization — that is intentional, since the point is an independent pipeline rather than a re-skin of the DESeq2 one.
acceptance_criteria: edgeR QL results table saved with logFC, logCPM, F, PValue, FDR
Significant gene counts reported for each method at BH-adjusted p < 0.05, plus the intersection size
Intersection saved as the high-confidence gene set; method-exclusive genes saved separately and labelled with the calling method
log2 fold change concordance between the two methods quantified over commonly tested genes
The union of the two methods is explicitly not presented as the result set
constraints: Use glmQLFit/glmQLFTest (quasi-likelihood F-test) — not the classic exact test and not the likelihood-ratio test
Same design and same contrast direction as T1S3: treated relative to control
BH adjustment at 0.05, matching the DESeq2 cutoff, so the comparison is like for like
Report the intersection as the high-confidence set; label single-method calls as secondary
caveats: A modest overlap at n=3 per group is expected and is itself the evidence about confidence — do not present disagreement as an error in either tool
Genes that DESeq2 set to NA via the Cook's outlier flag are untested there, so they cannot enter the intersection; account for them when computing overlap denominators
The two pipelines use different filters (independent filtering vs filterByExpr), so restrict concordance statistics to genes tested by both

grounding.reason: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test is the permitted alternative (M-0003) under R-0001@9a17 and is run here as the second method for the robustness check; the overlap is reported per R-0042@54e1. Choice stated: DESeq2 remains the primary result, edgeR the robustness check.

steps.name: DE report with power and confidence statement
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples', and what level of confidence do three replicates per group actually support?
steps.description: Assemble the final report. Order it so the confidence framing precedes the gene list: (1) the design and contrast as stated (condition, treated, control; 3 vs 3; single batch; no length offset applied to the Salmon gene-level counts, with the consequence that isoform-usage shifts can masquerade as differential expression); (2) the expected-power statement from T1S2 — the fold change detectable at 80% power with n=3 per group over the assumed BCV range, plus the plain statement that at three replicates a count model recovers only a minority of true effects and that absence from the list is not evidence of no change; (3) the fit diagnostics — MA plot on the shrunken LFC, dispersion plot, and the p-value histogram with its shape described; (4) the DESeq2 gene table ranked by shrunken log2 fold change, carrying unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE side by side, restricted to padj < 0.05; (5) the two-method overlap from T1S4, naming the intersection as the high-confidence set; (6) the reproducibility record — sessionInfo, all package versions, the design formula, the contrast, the thresholds, the number of genes tested and the number called per contrast, and any random seed used. If no gene reaches padj < 0.05, say so plainly and report the top genes by shrunken effect with their unadjusted p-values clearly marked as non-significant — do not relax the threshold to produce a list.
steps.context: Final deliverable for the question 'Which genes are differentially expressed between the treated and the control samples, and how confident can we be with three replicates per group?' on 3 treated vs 3 control human liver bulk RNA-seq samples, 12,000 genes.
acceptance_criteria: Power statement and the n=3 caution appear before the gene table, not as a footnote
Gene table carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken (apeglm) log2FoldChange and lfcSE together, ranked by the shrunken value, filtered by padj
MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histogram included with a one-line reading of each
Two-method overlap reported with per-method counts and the intersection named as the high-confidence set
Reproducibility record present: sessionInfo, package versions, design formula, contrast, thresholds, n tested, n DE
The lost length offset is stated as a limitation with its concrete consequence
An empty or near-empty significant set is reported as such, with no threshold relaxation
constraints: Rank genes by the shrunken log2 fold change, never by the unshrunken estimate alone
Keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit — shrinkage does not change the test
Name the shrinkage estimator (apeglm) in the table header
Do not loosen alpha, and do not present unadjusted p-values as evidence of differential expression
Do not add pathway or gene-set enrichment — the research question does not ask for it
caveats: Any biological interpretation of individual genes from a 3-vs-3 liver experiment is a hypothesis, not a finding; mark it as such
The single-batch design means no technical confounder can be tested for or adjusted; state this rather than implying the comparison is clean

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report step as a whole; its content follows the reporting claims returned for this situation (shrunken and unshrunken effects R-0085@bb37, fit diagnostics R-0087@3dcc, power statement at three replicates R-0094@6849, two-method overlap R-0042@54e1, reporting fields R-0041@059a, reproducibility record R-0086@becf)

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

With two or three replicates per group, the design step states the expected power of the test before the model. The tools of record for a power and sample size calculation, RNASeqPower and PROPER, are not in the pool here. Compute the power from the closed form of the sample size in terms of the depth, the biological coefficient of variation, the fold change, and the significance level, or take the dispersion from a pilot or a public dataset of the same tissue, and state the fold change that the design can find with 80 percent power. State that a larger replicate count raises the power more than a deeper sequencing does. The statement is a caution on the plan and not a reason to loosen the threshold.

If the smallest group holds three replicates, the test has low power. Both count models find only a small share of the true differentially expressed genes, most of them with a large fold change. Interpret the result with caution, and state the power limit in the report. Keep alpha at its default value, and do not change the threshold to compensate for the small design. A gene that is not in the list is not shown to be unchanged.
